reconcile.note: The Geneva annotators treat Zacharias and Elisabeth's law-keeping in Luke 1:6 as the fruit of faith rather than its ground, keeping righteousness rooted in faith alone.

discrepancy.note: Remsburg sets Paul's Galatians denial that the Law justifies against the very doers-of-the-law righteousness the Bible elsewhere affirms.

quotes.text: A man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, … for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified … If righteousness come by the law then Christ is dead in vain
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on justification by faith vs. the Law, Galatians 2:16, 21.

sides.snippet: the doers of the law will be justified
sides.verseText: For it isn't the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified

sides.snippet: if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!
sides.verseText: I don't make void the grace of God. For if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!\"
